Proof of Claim 5.2: the acceptance polynomial has degree 2t; Theorem 2.7 with s = 6 delta, n = 2t gives 1/(2 eps) <= sup|q| <= exp(48 t delta), hence t = Omega((1/delta) log(1/eps)). note: the constant 1/48 is read from the proof (Theorem 1.3 states only Omega). U_theta is a single-phase unitary family; applying Claim 5.3 to Grover-iterate access needs a theta-family with theta-independent eigenvectors (see counting-bound row). The arXiv v3 PDF footer says 'Accepted in Quantum 2026-05-05'; volume and article number are from the abs page.

source: Brassard, Hoyer, Mosca, Tapp, quant-ph/0005055v1, Theorem 12 (PDF fetched, text extracted)
claim_as_used_by_WS_k: |a~ - a| <= 2 pi k sqrt(a(1-a))/M + k^2 pi^2/M^2 with probability >= 8/pi^2 (k=1), > 1 - 1/(2(k-1)) (k>=2); any positive integer M
source_says: Theorem 12: for any positive integer k, Est_Amp(A, chi, M) outputs a~ with |a~ - a| <= 2 pi k sqrt(a(1-a))/M + k^2 pi^2/M^2 with probability at least 8/pi^2 when k=1 and greater than 1 - 1/(2(k-1)) for k>=2; it uses exactly M evaluations of f. The algorithm uses F_M for general M; the text adds that in practice M could be chosen a power of 2.
note: non-dyadic M is covered by the theorem (it needs an exact or error-budgeted QFT over Z_M). Call convention: Lambda_M(Q) applies Q^j for j <= M-1, so M-1 controlled-Q per shot (program convention); BHMT counts M evaluations of f.

source_says: Lemma 4 states (23) with 'probability of error less than delta' using N calls to U or U^dagger. App. D derives it with approximations: Gaussian approximation of the normalisation (D5)-(D6), Bessel asymptotics (D7)-(D9), a tail bound with sin replaced by 1 (D10), arcsinh(alpha) ~ ln(2 alpha) (D11); (D13) is written with '~=' and (D14)/(D15) carry O(lnln) remainders. Window index m = -N..N (D2); 'the number of calls to U or U^dagger is N'.
note: the derivation is approximate and asymptotic, so it gives no certified finite worst-case constant; WS-k's 'no explicit constant' reading is correct. Lemma 4's 'a' is the amplitude in U|0,0> = a|psi0,0> + ...; WS-k uses the phase-error reading, which is what App. D derives.

source: Patel, Tan, Subasi, Sornborger, arXiv:2403.18927v3, Remark 1, Theorems 1-3, p.10-11 (PDF fetched)
claim_as_used_by_WS_k: DPSS taper is the exact average-case optimum; Thm 2 non-asymptotic m = ceil(log2(175(log(10/delta)+1)^2 + 1)) + 1 extra ancillas, average-case only; Thm 3 asymptotic
source_says: Remark 1: averaging over the phase offset makes the problem continuous and the DPSS taper optimal (average case). Theorem 2 (non-asymptotic): m = ceil(log2(ceil(175(log(10/eps_bar)+1)^2) + 1)) + 1 additional ancilla qubits suffice for AVERAGE success probability >= 1 - eps_bar, via the [KRD21] eigenvalue bound (32). Theorem 3 (asymptotic): m ~ ceil(log2 log(1/eps_bar)) from Slepian asymptotics, valid only for N >= N_0 with N_0 unspecified.
note: WS-k dropped the inner ceiling (negligible). Both theorems are average-case over the phase; Thm 3 has no finite constant.

claim_as_used_by_WS_k: (1-delta)K <= 2N+1 for N controlled Q/Q^-1 calls via the Mande-de Wolf Claim 5.3 degree argument; k_LB 1.70 (B4x12) / 1.85 (B8x52) at delta=0.01, e=0.45eps, support class
check: Re-derived. (i) Hard family A_theta = R_y(2 theta) on one payoff qubit (payoff S*Bernoulli(sin^2 theta)); Q_theta, Q_theta^-1, direction-select and controlled versions all have theta-independent eigenvectors with eigenvalues in {1, e^{+-2i theta}}, so Claim 5.3's premise holds for this family and the final state lies in span{e^{2ij theta}|v_j>: |j|<=N}. (ii) One copy of A|0> adds a factor e^{+-i theta}: odd exponents only, dim <= 2N+2. (iii) Disjoint success sets for K means spaced >2e and sum_i <psi_i|E_i|psi_i> <= tr(P_V) give (1-delta)K <= dim V. Intermediate measurements are deferred without changing the call count.
result: verified with a negligible correction: with one free copy of A|0> the bound is ((1-delta)K-2)/2 (k_LB 1.691 vs 1.695 at B4x12 eps=0.1; identical to 4 digits at eps<=0.01). With A/A^dagger access at half a Q each the bound halves (0.85/0.93).
scope: black-box (A or Q) access, worst case over all payoff laws on [0, 38.818]; expressed in units of the task sigma. Does not bind white-box estimators (F04/F05/F20) or estimators promised a narrower class (mean-bounded class: 0.156/0.159).
label: modelled (rigorous analytic)

statement: An explicit, non-asymptotic, worst-case-over-amplitude bound: for every a in [0,1], N <= c(delta)/Delta + c0 controlled Q / Q^-1 (or direction-select) calls give |phi_hat - 2 theta| <= Delta with probability >= 1 - delta, for delta = 0.003 (or 0.01) and c(delta) near 4.2 (3.5), with every finite-size term (readout grid, window-state preparation, QFT precision) inside delta. Equivalently a QSP/ChebAE schedule with a proven worst-case 99% coverage and explicit constant. Target: k about 8-9 (with U1/U2 credits) or 24-26 (without).
